 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Atlanta Dream finished the 2026 WNBA season with a 30-14 record, good for fourth in the standings. They went on to sweep the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty in the first two rounds of the playoffs, advancing to the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries.
 Unfortunately, Angel Reese and company couldn't overcome Golden State . While the Dream were able to push the series to the full seven games, they ended up losing 4-3. In the deciding Game 7, Gabby Williams exploded for 30 points to lead the Valkyries to a 68-63 victory.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The WNBA Finals exposed the Dream's major weakness: their bench. While Atlanta has a deadly starting unit featuring Reese, Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada and Naz Hillmon, its bench unit left much to be desired. Even the addition of DeWanna Bonner late in the season didn't solve the problem.
 During the Finals, the Dream's bench was outscored by the Valkyries' second unit in six of the seven games they played. In Game 5, which gave Golden State a 3-2 series lead, the Valkyries won the bench scoring 15-4.
 That being said, Sabreena Merchant of The Athletic emphasized that acquiring a "trusted depth player" should be the Dream's priority this offseason.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In her analysis, the WNBA reporter floated the idea of the Dream potentially targeting Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington to address that need.
 Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington looks on from the bench.Jerome Miron-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect
 Carrington averaged 8.8 points and 3.1 rebounds in 11 games for the Sky last season. She also played alongside Bonner for four seasons with the Connecticut Sun.
 "What Atlanta needs is a little more bench depth to spell its starters, but they have to be players who Karl Smesko will trust to put on the court," Merchant explained. "Brionna Jones should factor into the rotation after missing most of 2026. Looking beyond the existing roster, DiJonai Carrington also fits that mold if she's healthy; she already has familiarity with Jones, assistant coach Brandi Poole and DeWanna Bonner if the veteran sticks around."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Carrington is set to become an unrestricted free agent this offseason. Sure enough, it will be interesting to see what she decides to do with her career.
